claims.text: DFT with machine-learning corrections can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach can predict lattice thermal conductivity with less than 10% error relative to experimental values.
The target materials are high-entropy alloys in a solid-solution state.
The intervention is the application of DFT with machine-learning corrections to predict lattice thermal conductivity.
Lattice structure and chemical composition mediate the approach's thermal-conductivity prediction.
The unique lattice structure and chemical composition of high-entropy alloys reduce phonon scattering.
Reduced phonon scattering is proposed to produce lattice thermal conductivity below 5 W/mK.
The identified high-entropy alloys will have lattice thermal conductivity below 5 W/mK.
Traditional alloys used in thermal-insulation applications provide the baseline for comparison.
The approach is limited to high-entropy alloys having a single-phase FCC or BCC structure.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the particular high-entropy-alloy composition and structure.
The proposed benchmark experimentally measures lattice thermal conductivity, composition, and structure for alloys predicted to have low thermal conductivity.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if measured lattice thermal conductivity is more than 15% higher than the predicted value.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims less than 10% prediction error, but the falsification rule only rejects predictions that are more than 15% too low. Errors from 10% to 15%, and errors greater than 10% in the opposite direction, violate the accuracy claim without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
